newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialist says EU needs do more for jobs.
newsitem.headline: French Socialist says EU needs do more for jobs.

text.p: France's new Socialist party leader Francois Hollande said a European Union deal on Monday to boost jobs and growth was a step forward but that Paris would be demanding more action on employment.

The French government "has got things moving. It has not yet obtained everything it wanted", he told RTL radio after EU leaders in Amsterdam approved a budget stability pact and a resolution on boosting jobs and growth.
"There will be other efforts to be made, Amsterdam is not the final stage...I hope we will be able to continue to make our partners put jobs at the heart of European construction," he said.

EU leaders swept aside a row over the future of the bloc's plans for a single currency from 1999 by agreeing a pact to put action for jobs and growth on a par with stringent limits on budget deficits.
The deal was hailed as a breakthrough by France, Britain and the Dutch summit hosts.

Hollande said Germany, France's main partner in the EU, had been reluctant to spend cash on jobs. "On jobs, the essential blockage is over the German will not to devote extra spending towards employment policies," he said.
Hollande succeeded new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin as party leader after the left swept to power in France's parliamentary election two weeks ago.

Hollande said Paris had not changed the budget stability pact agreed in Dublin in December by Paris's centre-right government of the time. "It remains as rigorous as it was. It's a shame. But France's word was given in December," he said.
He said the agreement would yield "a better coordination of economic policies so that growth, jobs are at the heart of European construction".
